sentences.text: ORDER This is third application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the BNSS for grant of regular bail.

The applicant has been arrested in connection with Crime No.306/2024 registered at Police Station Kailaras, District Morena for offence under Sections 376, 376(2)(n) & 506 of IPC and Sections 376(2)(L) & Section 506 Part II of IPC and Section 5(L), 5(k) and 5(J)(ii)/6(1) of POCSO Act.

His first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 19.09.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.No.37096/2024 and his second bail application was dismissed as withdrawn with a liberty to file afresh after examination of prosecutrix vide order dated 22.11.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.No.46515/2024.
2. Allegation against the present applicant is that he committed rape upon the prosecutrix/victim.
3 . Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
He is in custody since 14.07.2024.

It is further submitted that after dismissal of the second bail application the statements NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20733 2 MCRC-14547-2025 of prosecutrix, her father and mother have been recorded before the trial Court.
Prosecutrix in her statement has stated that she wants to live with applicant/accused.
It seems that prosecutrix the prosecutrix was consensual relationship with the present applicant.
There is no criminal antecedent against the present applicant.

Charge-sheet has been filed and the investigation Dilshad Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93730483/
1 is over, therefore, custodial interrogation is no longer required.

sentences.text: DNA report is found to be negative.
Applicant is a permanent resident of District Morena (M.P.), therefore, there is no possibility of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
Applicant undertakes to cooperate in trial as well as the investigation and would make himself available as and when required.
Under these grounds, counsel prayed for bail.
4. On the other hand, learned State counsel vehemently opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.

5. Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary.
6.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) along with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/Committal Court.
8. E- copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance.
9. Certified copy as per rules.
